# Code.org

> Free K–12 computer science and AI curriculum, student learning tools, and teacher professional learning.

Code.org is a nonprofit education platform that provides standards-aligned computer science and AI learning experiences for students, classroom-ready curriculum for teachers, professional development, and advocacy resources to expand access to CS education.

## Core Platform
- [Home](https://code.org/): Main entry point for Code.org curriculum, student activities, teacher resources, and initiatives.
- [Students](https://code.org/students): Student hub for courses, self-paced learning, projects, and computer science career exploration.
- [Teach](https://code.org/teach): Teacher hub for curriculum, lesson materials, classroom implementation guidance, and training.
- [About](https://code.org/about): Organization mission, impact, leadership, partners, and background on Code.org’s work.
- [Projects](https://studio.code.org/projects): Creative coding workspace for building and sharing apps, games, animations, and more.
- [Hour of Code](https://hourofcode.com/): Global campaign with introductory coding activities for classrooms, families, and events.

## Curriculum
- [Curriculum Catalog](https://code.org/curriculum): Overview of Code.org courses and instructional pathways by grade band and topic.
- [Elementary School Curriculum](https://code.org/curriculum/elementary-school): CS fundamentals and elementary learning pathways with unplugged and online lessons.
- [Middle School Curriculum](https://code.org/curriculum/middle-school): Middle grades courses focused on core CS concepts and problem solving.
- [High School Curriculum](https://code.org/curriculum/high-school): High school offerings including foundational, web, game, data, and AI courses.
- [Computer Science Fundamentals](https://code.org/curriculum/computer-science-fundamentals): Introductory elementary curriculum teaching sequencing, loops, events, and basic programming.
- [Computer Science Discoveries](https://code.org/curriculum/computer-science-discoveries): Middle school course covering problem solving, web development, data, and physical computing.
- [Computer Science Principles](https://code.org/curriculum/computer-science-principles): AP-aligned course introducing computing concepts, programming, data, and the internet.
- [CSAIF: Foundations of AI](https://code.org/curriculum/artificial-intelligence-foundations): High school AI curriculum on machine learning, ethics, and real-world applications.

## AI Learning
- [Artificial Intelligence](https://code.org/artificial-intelligence): Central landing page for AI education programs, lessons, and classroom resources.
- [AI Education Hub](https://code.org/ai): Collection of AI activities, explainers, and teaching resources for students and educators.
- [How AI Works](https://code.org/ai/how-ai-works): Introductory materials explaining core AI concepts and model behavior.
- [AI for Oceans](https://code.org/oceans): Interactive activity teaching machine learning concepts through ocean cleanup scenarios.
- [Dance Party: AI Edition](https://code.org/dance): Creative activity combining coding and AI-themed interactive experiences.
- [AI Foundations Curriculum](https://code.org/curriculum/artificial-intelligence-foundations): Full course materials for teaching AI concepts in high school classrooms.
- [AI Literacy Day](https://code.org/ai-literacy-day): Event resources and activities supporting broad AI literacy participation.

## Teacher Resources
- [Professional Learning](https://code.org/professional-learning): Workshops, facilitator-led programs, and self-paced training for teachers.
- [Educate for the Future](https://code.org/teach/artificial-intelligence): Teacher-facing AI education overview with classroom implementation resources.
- [District Program](https://code.org/districts): Support for districts adopting and scaling computer science education programs.
- [Curriculum Values](https://code.org/values): Principles guiding inclusive, equitable, and accessible curriculum design.
- [Teacher Community](https://forum.code.org/): Community forum for educators to ask questions and share classroom practices.
- [Help Center](https://support.code.org/): Support articles for teachers, students, accounts, sections, and classroom tools.

## Student Learning and Tools
- [Studio](https://studio.code.org/): Interactive learning environment for courses, puzzles, labs, and student projects.
- [Course Catalog](https://studio.code.org/courses): Browse available student courses and grade-level learning pathways.
- [App Lab](https://studio.code.org/projects/applab): Build apps with JavaScript in Code.org’s browser-based development environment.
- [Game Lab](https://studio.code.org/projects/gamelab): Create games and animations using JavaScript and block-based programming.
- [Sprite Lab](https://studio.code.org/projects/spritelab): Design interactive stories and games with sprites and blocks.
- [Play Lab](https://studio.code.org/projects/playlab): Introductory environment for creating simple interactive stories and games.
- [Artist](https://studio.code.org/projects/artist): Visual coding environment for drawing and geometry-based programming activities.
- [Python Lab](https://studio.code.org/projects/pythonlab): Browser-based Python environment for text-based programming activities.

## Labs and Development Environments
- [App Lab Docs](https://studio.code.org/docs/ide/applab): Reference and guidance for building apps in App Lab.
- [Game Lab Docs](https://studio.code.org/docs/ide/gamelab): Documentation for animation, sprites, and game programming in Game Lab.
- [Sprite Lab Docs](https://studio.code.org/docs/ide/spritelab): Documentation for block-based interactive projects in Sprite Lab.
- [Web Lab Docs](https://studio.code.org/docs/ide/weblab): Guidance for creating websites with HTML and CSS in Web Lab.
- [Python Lab Docs](https://studio.code.org/docs/ide/pythonlab): Documentation for Python Lab features and classroom use.
- [Java Lab Docs](https://studio.code.org/docs/ide/javalab): Documentation for Java Lab programming and course integration.
- [Maker Toolkit Docs](https://studio.code.org/docs/maker/start/): Setup and usage documentation for physical computing with Maker Toolkit.

## Documentation and Reference
- [Documentation Home](https://studio.code.org/docs/): Central documentation index for labs, APIs, and classroom tools.
- [App Lab Concepts](https://studio.code.org/docs/concepts/app-lab/): Concept guides for events, variables, functions, and UI design in App Lab.
- [Game Lab Concepts](https://studio.code.org/docs/concepts/game-lab/): Concept guides for sprites, animation, conditionals, and game logic.
- [Web Lab Concepts](https://studio.code.org/docs/concepts/web-lab/): Concept guides for HTML, CSS, and website creation in Web Lab.
- [JavaScript Concepts](https://studio.code.org/docs/concepts/javascript/): Introductory JavaScript explanations used across Code.org programming environments.
- [Patterns](https://studio.code.org/docs/concepts/patterns/): Reusable programming patterns for common classroom coding tasks.
- [Java Lab API](https://studio.code.org/docs/ide/javalab/classes/Neighborhood/): Reference example for Java Lab classes and methods.
- [App Lab API](https://studio.code.org/docs/ide/applab/expressions/getProperty): API-style reference for App Lab functions and expressions.

## Advocacy and Policy
- [Promote Computer Science](https://code.org/promote): Advocacy resources for expanding CS education in schools and states.
- [Advocacy Coalition](https://advocacy.code.org/): Coalition site with policy priorities, campaigns, and state-level advocacy resources.
- [State of CS Report](https://advocacy.code.org/stateofcs): Data and reporting on access to computer science education across the U.S.
- [Policy Maker Resources](https://code.org/yourschool): Tools and information for school and district leaders evaluating CS access.
- [Why Computer Science](https://code.org/why-cs): Evidence and rationale for offering computer science to all students.

## Organization and Support
- [Donate](https://code.org/donate): Donation page supporting free curriculum, teacher training, and access initiatives.
- [Careers](https://code.org/about/jobs): Open roles and employment information for joining Code.org.
- [Leadership](https://code.org/about/leadership): Profiles of organizational leadership and board members.
- [Partners](https://code.org/about/partners): Partner organizations supporting Code.org programs and initiatives.
- [Contact](https://code.org/contact): Contact options for support, media, partnerships, and general inquiries.
- [Privacy Policy](https://code.org/privacy): Privacy practices governing Code.org websites, tools, and services.
- [Terms of Service](https://code.org/tos): Terms governing use of Code.org platforms, content, and services.
